list.name: app
list.label: Application
list.query: (kind:log OR kind:measurement OR kind:exception) | uniq by (service.name)

panels.title: RUM signal volume by kind
panels.description: Every Faro payload lands here as one of three kinds: log (console/custom logs), measurement (Web Vitals and other numeric metrics), or exception (uncaught JS errors). Query shape verified 2026-08-24 against a real Faro payload — kind, _time bucketing, and the stats-by-kind grouping are all proven working, not guessed.

targets.expr: service.name:in(${app:csv}) | stats by (_time:1m, kind) count() as count

panels.title: JS error rate (uncaught exceptions)
panels.description: Count of kind:exception records over time. This is what a shipped frontend regression looks like — a sudden step up from zero.

targets.expr: service.name:in(${app:csv}) kind:exception | stats by (_time:1m) count() as errors

panels.title: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint, ms, avg)
panels.description: Web Vitals arrive as kind:measurement, type:web-vitals, with each metric stored twice in the message text (a plain key and a value_-prefixed key) — the value_ prefixed one is what these panels extract. Confirmed 2026-08-24: a chained single-field extract per metric works reliably; a single extract call with all four fields in one pattern does NOT (returns NaN) — each field needs its own extract pipe. The LAST field in a chain also needs its own trailing-space delimiter, same as every other field — omitting it let the pattern capture past the number into the next key=value pair, which is what originally produced a NaN on TTFB specifically until this was caught and fixed.

targets.expr: service.name:in(${app:csv}) kind:measurement type:web-vitals | extract "value_LCP=<LCP> " | stats avg(LCP) as avg_lcp
service.name:in(${app:csv}) kind:measurement type:web-vitals | extract "value_FCP=<FCP> " | stats avg(FCP) as avg_fcp
service.name:in(${app:csv}) kind:measurement type:web-vitals | extract "value_CLS=<CLS> " | stats avg(CLS) as avg_cls

panels.title: TTFB (Time to First Byte, ms, avg)
panels.description: Confirmed the trailing-space delimiter matters here specifically — this field sits last in the raw message before app_name=..., so without its own trailing space the extract pattern captured into the next key=value pair instead of stopping at the number, and this panel returned NaN until that was fixed.

targets.expr: service.name:in(${app:csv}) kind:measurement type:web-vitals | extract "value_TTFB=<TTFB> " | stats avg(TTFB) as avg_ttfb
